classification.classification_note: The reproduced fault is not the later `sweep_axis` cleanup issue from the same patch set. The saved ASan trace exercises the `Q->h <= 0.` error path in `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos`, where `pj_default_destructor(P, ...)` frees the `PJ` object and execution then falls through to read `P->phi0`.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 25-byte text blob `+h\xff\xff\t+proj=geos\n+pj=geos\n`. In `standard_fuzzer`, the first line alone is passed to `pj_init_plus()`, so proj.4 tokenizes `+h\xff\xff\t+proj=geos` into the malformed parameter token `h\xff\xff` plus the valid projection selector `proj=geos`. `pj_init_ctx` therefore still dispatches to the geostationary projection setup, but when `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos` asks `pj_param(..., "dh")` for the mandatory `h` value, `pj_param` requires the stored parameter to end immediately after `h` or continue with `=`, and the malformed token `h\xff\xff` fails that exact-match test. The numeric lookup consequently falls back to the default `0.0`, making `Q->h <= 0.` true. On the reproduced path, `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos` then calls `pj_default_destructor(P, PJD_ERR_H_LESS_THAN_ZERO)`, which frees `P->params`, `P->opaque`, and the 648-byte `PJ` object itself, but the function does not return. It immediately falls through to `if (P->phi0 != 0.0)` and reads `phi0` from the freed `PJ`, producing the saved ASan heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/PJ_geos.c:202`. The relevant hunk in the staged `patch.diff` fixes this path by changing each early error cleanup in `PJ_geos.c` to `return pj_default_destructor(...)`; the same commit also removes the unrelated `sweep_axis` member.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled first projection string. While splitting on `+` and whitespace, this statement emits the malformed token `h\xff\xff` and the valid selector token `proj=geos`, which are the only first-line values that later drive the vulnerable geos initialization path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the 25-byte blob `2b 68 ff ff 09 2b 70 72 6f 6a 3d 67 65 6f 73 0a 2b 70 6a 3d 67 65 6f 73 0a`. In the first `pj_init_plus()` call, `definition` is just the bytes before the first newline: `+h\xff\xff\t+proj=geos`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the malformed `h\xff\xff` token becomes the concrete trigger value. Because the preceding exact-match test rejects `h\xff\xff` as neither `h` nor `h=...`, the missing decimal option `dh` defaults to `0.0`, which `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos` stores in `Q->h` and uses for the error branch.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Derived from the first-line token `h\xff\xff` parsed from the staged witness; that token begins with `h` but fails `pj_param`'s exact option-name check.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The `Q->h <= 0.` error path frees the live `PJ` object through `pj_default_destructor(P, ...)` but does not return afterward, so the local `P` remains a dangling pointer and subsequent statements operate on freed memory.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this exact statement to `return pj_default_destructor (P, PJD_ERR_H_LESS_THAN_ZERO);`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After step 6 has freed `P`, this branch condition immediately reads the `phi0` field from the freed 648-byte `PJ` allocation, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free READ 8 at `src/PJ_geos.c:202:12`.

parser_admitted.description: The malformed first token does not reject the definition outright because the same parameter list still contains the valid selector `proj=geos`. `pj_init_ctx` therefore admits the projection definition and dispatches into the vulnerable geos-specific setup.

coarse_trace.summary: proj.4 tokenizes the first fuzzed projection string into `h\xff\xff` and `proj=geos`, copies those tokens into the parameter list, and selects the geos projection initializer.
When geos setup asks for `dh`, the malformed token fails `pj_param`'s exact option-name match and the decimal lookup defaults to `0.0`.
The `Q->h <= 0.` error branch calls `pj_default_destructor` on the live `PJ` object but falls through instead of returning.
The next statement reads `P->phi0` from the freed `PJ`, matching the saved ASan heap-use-after-free report.

fine_trace.note: Source. While tokenizing the first projection string `+h\xff\xff\t+proj=geos`, this statement emits `argv[0] = "h\xff\xff"` at the leading `+` and later emits `argv[1] = "proj=geos"` after the tab delimiter trims the malformed first token.

Copies those attacker-derived tokens into the linked `paralist` consumed by all later `pj_param` lookups. On the crashing path the list begins with `param = "h\xff\xff"` and then `param = "proj=geos"`.

Because step 2 still provides `proj=geos`, `pj_init_ctx` dispatches to the geos constructor. `proj(0)` allocates the `PJ` object later identified by ASan as the 648-byte freed region, and `PIN->params = start` makes the malformed parameter list reachable from that object during geos setup.

When `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos` requests `pj_param(P->ctx, P->params, "dh").f`, the exact-match test at lines 49-50 rejects the stored token `h\xff\xff` because the byte after `h` is neither `\0` nor `=`, so the missing decimal option falls through to the default `0.0` return.
Stores the step-4 result into `Q->h`; here `Q->h = 0.0`, so the `<= 0.` predicate is true and the geos setup enters its error-cleanup path.

Invalidates the live `PJ` from step 3 by freeing its parameter list, opaque payload, and the `PJ` object itself. Because this destructor call is not returned from, `P` remains a dangling local and execution continues into subsequent field accesses.
Sink. The immediate fallthrough after step 6 reads `phi0` from the freed `PJ`, which is exactly the heap-use-after-free READ 8 reported by the saved ASan trace at `src/PJ_geos.c:202:12`.

poc.trigger: Feed the exact staged 25-byte file `+h\xff\xff\t+proj=geos\n+pj=geos\n` to `standard_fuzzer`. The harness passes only the first line to `pj_init_plus()`, and the crash occurs during that first projection initialization before the destination projection or coordinates are processed.

format.name: proj.4 standard_fuzzer 3-line text blob
format.contract: An exact 25-byte text witness whose first line is `+h\xff\xff\t+proj=geos`, second line is `+pj=geos`, and third line is empty. The trigger relies on the first line tokenizing into the malformed parameter `h\xff\xff` plus `proj=geos`, so `pj_param(..., "dh").f` defaults to `0.0` and `pj_projection_specific_setup_geos` takes the `Q->h <= 0.` destructor path.
